author: opencode-worker-4
text: Claimed-and-released by worker-4 (2026-08-31): the Rust slot-claim COSE migration cannot land independently — it is one leg of a coordinated three-implementation wire-format change (Rust resources.rs + Python slot_claim.py + C gcp_trust.c, plus gcp_slot_claim.json regeneration), because the three stacks already sign THREE incompatible transcript formats today (Rust domain-prefixed transcript slot.rs:723; C b'SLOT_CLAIM:'+message gcp_trust.h:59; Python canonical-CBOR string-keyed map) and the vectors file is Python-only and self-referential (slot_claim_basic hex embeds 0xbf fragments cbor2 cannot decode). GOOD NEWS for the implementer: the complete strict COSE_Sign1 machinery is already proven in this very crate — tunnel_auth.rs decode_and_hash_sign1 (:553, exact-length bstr reads, PROTECTED=a1013a00010000, UnsupportedAlgorithm vs MalformedCbor discrimination), signature_digest (Sig_structure writer :511-523), and the payload map decoder pattern (:581+). Plan: (1) Mark or the 16-family owner adjudicates the coordinated landing (payload keys 1-7 mapping per spec/08: slots array, superframe_epoch, mode, expiry, gateway_iid bstr(8), claim_seq, ordinal — gateway_count OFF the wire); (2) regenerate vectors with golden signatures; (3) port tunnel_auth's decode_and_hash_sign1+signature_digest into resources.rs SlotClaim::decode/encode (protected bstr check, kid==verifying-key IID binding like l1qw.26.2.1); (4) keep RawSlotClaim/verifier as the post-decode type; (5) Python .16.1 mirrors with the shared cose_* helpers; (6) C .16.4 follows. Releasing unclaimed — recommend the three children + .16.4 be executed by one worker in one session.
